newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close down after Dow dips.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close down after Dow dips.

text.p: The Australian share market closed lower on Tuesday after the Dow continued its downtrend.
The only local bright spot was a gold sector that received a pick-me-up from a firmer bullion price in offshore markets.
The All Ordinaries index lost 18.8 points to 2,404.2.
Resuming from a holiday long weekend, the local market played catchup to two days of Wall Street weakness and losses were widely spread.
"It is the Dow hanging over our heads again," said Jim Tredenick, senior dealer at Brisbane-based brokerage, Nevitts Ltd, adding that heavier losses would not have surprised.
"I thought it might have come off a bit more, but overall our market hasn't done too badly."

Other players agreed, noting that the March share index futures contract (SPI) had settled at a discount to the benchmark All Ordinaries index, with traders cautious ahead of U.S. wages data due later on Tuesday and local inflation data due Wednesaday.
"It's been a Dow-driven day," said a Sydney broker.
"The SPI seems set at a discount as traders short or cut positions ahead of the U.S. tonight."
In the golds, Acacia Resources, up 2.8 percent to A$2.19 (US$1.69), Plutonic also up 2.8 percent to A$5.15, and Normandy Mining, whose scrip added 2.5 percent to A$1.63, were the pick.
Elsewhere, shares in metals recycler Simsmetal lost 29 cents to close at A$6.99 after posting a 43 percent lower first half net profit of A$$14.07 million.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
